newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Political uncertainty sends Israeli shares lower.
newsitem.headline: Political uncertainty sends Israeli shares lower.

text.p: Shaken by a political scandal that threatens to bring down the Israeli government, Tel Aviv shares opened lower on Thursday.
The benchmark Mishtanim Index opened down 1.05 percent or 2.66 points at 251.63 while the Maof 25 index fell 1.03 percent at 261.24.
The market opened with almost 80 million shekels in supply versus only three million in demand.
Analysts said the market would remain unstable with foreign investors sidelined until the fate of the government becomes clear.

"The market was extremely resilient until yesterday. If it blows over the market will resume momentum but if there are new elections that period will be very uncertain," said Daniella Finn of Batucha Securities.
Police said on Wednesday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should be charged with fraud and breach of trust in an influence-peddling scandal.
An aide to Netanyahu said on Thursday he did not believe the state prosecutor would implement the police recommendation.

An exception to Thursday's decline was Koor Industries, which opened up 0.25 percent to 307.26 shekels. Finn noted that its shares on Wall Street traded in record turnover on Wednesday of $11.5 million and closed up 1/4 at $18.
Finn said she believed a foreign buyer was behind the unusual volume.
